signals.text: Normal pace of buying and selling (RSI 44)
signals.why: RSI is 44 on a 0–100 scale (below 30 = fell fast, above 70 = rose fast).

signals.text: Unusually busy trading on the last day (6.5× normal)
signals.why: 32,32,486 shares traded vs a 20-day average of 4,94,330.

lines.text: Earns 31% a year on all the money it uses
lines.why: For every ₹100 of shareholders' money and loans in the business, it made ₹31 of operating profit last year (better than 86% of Construction & EPC). Past years: very uneven; recent trend improving. Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 15, weak < 10 (default rule, all sectors).
For every ₹100 of shareholders' money, it has borrowed ₹45 (better than 38% of Construction & EPC). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≤ 1, weak > 1.5.

lines.text: Profit is not fully turning into cash
lines.why: For every ₹100 of reported profit in recent years, ₹-80 actually came in as cash (better than 9% of Construction & EPC). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 0.8, weak < 0.5 (default rule, all sectors).
On ₹365 crore of yearly sales, about ₹253 crore is waiting to be collected at any time (better than 6% of Construction & EPC). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≤ 120, weak > 180.
₹100 of sales 3 years ago is about ₹1803 now (better than all other Construction & EPC). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 10, weak < 0 (default rule, all sectors).

valuation.text: Price tag: in line with its close peers
valuation.why: You pay ₹24 for every ₹1 of yearly profit. Colour from close peers (Farm & Heavy Construction Machinery (Construction), 6 stocks): middle half 17.1–28.2 (band rule PROXY).

flags.text: Check: the accounts resemble past earnings-manipulation cases (Beneish M-score)
flags.why: M-score 0.05 is above the −1.78 line. This is a statistical hint, not proof, and the score is not yet validated on Indian companies: read the annual report's notes on receivables, margins and cash flow before trusting the profits.

flags.text: Profit is running well ahead of cash coming in
flags.why: (Profit − operating cash flow) is 23.0% of total assets; above 10% is a warning.
Only ₹-80 of cash came in for every ₹100 of reported profit over recent years (below ₹50 is a red flag).

flags.text: Thinly traded – hard to buy or sell without moving the price
flags.why: Typical day: about ₹1.5 crore traded (we exclude below ₹5 crore).

fund.note: Cash flow matters most here: profits with negative operating cash flow for 3+ years is a red flag.

lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: would probably pass (1 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: For every ₹100 it owes within a year, it holds ₹307 of cash, stock and dues coming in.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹36 cr vs working capital ₹121 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years
ch.r: Positive earnings in each of the last 10 years
ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: A gap of about 105 months without a dividend (2016-11 to 2025-09).

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years
ch.w: Not enough EPS history.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹35 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.
You pay ₹6.35 for every ₹1 of net worth.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)
ch.w: With EPS ₹0.7 and book value ₹3 per share, Graham's ceiling price is ₹7.

ch.r: No loss in 10 years
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see.

ch.n: Doesn't eat its cash in capex

ch.w: No operating cash to fund capex.

ch.r: Share count up no more than 5% over the years we have

ch.r: Candid, sensible with capital, no governance red flags

ch.w: Our automatic checks are a starting point only.
q: Do they admit mistakes in the annual report letter?

ch.r: Debt-to-equity below 0.35

ch.r: EPS growth 20–25% a year

ch.r: Insider buying is a green flag

ch.r: A buyback is a green flag

ch.n: Not a hot stock in a hot industry

ch.r: Management talks openly about problems

lenses.sp: Ranks every company on 'cheap' and 'good' and buys the best combined ranks.

ch.r: Earnings yield (EBIT ÷ EV) in the top 30%

ch.r: EBIT ÷ (working capital + net fixed assets) in the top 30%

ch.n: Near the top of the Magic Formula list

ch.w: Greenblatt's method (STATED) buys the best 20–30 combined ranks; 'top 10%' is our cut-off.

lenses.sp: Nine quick tests of whether the business got healthier this year than last.

ch.r: Operating cash flow > net profit

ch.r: Long-term debt ÷ assets lower than last year

ch.r: Gross margin higher than last year
ch.w: Keeps more of each sale after direct costs.

ch.r: Share count not higher than last year
ch.w: Owners weren't diluted.

ch.r: Sales ÷ assets higher than last year
ch.w: Squeezing more sales out of what it owns.
